rows.speaker: أبي وعبد الله
rows.claim: Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh read وعَبَدوا in the plural; ʿAbd Allāh’s companions instead read وعَبَدَ الطاغوت as a verb, annexed to al-Ṭāghūt and glossed as serving it.
rows.anchor: وهي في قراءة أبي وعبد الله (وعبدوا) على الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وعَبَدَ الطاغوت can mean servants of al-Ṭāghūt, with the feminine ending dropped in annexation; a poet’s ولاها for ولاتها illustrates the omission.
rows.anchor: يريد عبدة الطاغوت فيحذف الهاء لمكان الإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If عَبَد is a dialectal form like حذر or عجل, that reading is valid; otherwise its form is only poetic license and cannot be used in Qurʾānic recitation.
rows.anchor: وهذا في الشعر يجوز لضرورة القوافي، فأما في القراءة فلا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews’ claim that God’s hand is tied means He withholds spending and bestowal, as in the injunction not to keep one’s hand tied to one’s neck when spending.
rows.anchor: ممسكة عن الإنفاق والإسباغ علينا

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh’s reading has بسطان; Arabic also describes a person as meeting a friend with an open or expansive face.
rows.anchor: بل يداه مبسوطتان وفي حرف عبد الله بل يداه بسطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having provision from above and beneath means rain from the sky and plants and fruits from the earth.
rows.anchor: من قطر السماء ونبات الأرض من ثمارها وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible sense is abundance or comprehensiveness, like saying someone enjoys good from head to foot.
rows.anchor: إن هذا على وجه التوسعة كما تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative كثير منهم may carry the repeated verbs over to many of them, meaning that many became blind and deaf.
rows.anchor: فقد يكون رفع الكثير من جهتين إحداهما أن تكر الفعل عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, عموا وصموا can be plural verbs whose subject is كثير, as in the poetic construction أهلي فكلهم ألوم and the expression قاموا قومك.
rows.anchor: وإن شئت جعلت عموا وصموا فعلا للكثير كما قال الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third parse treats كثير as a verbal noun; on that interpretation the accusative is also correct.
rows.anchor: وإن شئت جعلت الكثير مصدرا فقلت أي ذلك كثير منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic uses a direct reflexive expression with complete verbs (قتلتم أنفسكم; ظلموا أنفسهم), but defective cognition verbs take a pronoun attached to the verb (أظنني خارجا), distinguishing verbs that may be omitted from those that cannot.
rows.anchor: في الأفعال التامة غير ما يقولون في الناقصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān says أن رآه استغنى rather than رأى نفسه; poetry can use a direct object with a complete verb, but forms such as عدمتني are not standard speech.
rows.anchor: أن رآه استغنى ولم يقل: رأى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here فلولا means فهلا; when followed by one nominative noun it has conditional لولا’s sense, but without a noun it is interrogative. لوما behaves the same way.
rows.anchor: فإذا رأيت بعدها اسما واحدا مرفوعا فهو بمعنى لولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opened doors are provisions and rain, worldly good given as a trial; this resembles the sudden punishment after the earth’s adornment and the promise of abundant water to those persisting on the way of shirk.
rows.anchor: يعني أبواب الرزق والمطر وهو الخير في الدنيا لنفتنهم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭarīqa here means the way of shirk: had they persisted in it, God would have given them abundant water as a trial.
rows.anchor: والطريقة طريقة الشرك أي لو استمروا عليها فعلنا ذلك بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every community has a festival for amusement, while Muḥammad’s community has festivals of piety, prayer, takbīr, and goodness.
rows.anchor: ليس من قوم إلا ولهم عيد فهم يلهون في أعيادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تبسل means to be held hostage; Arabs also use بسل for something forbidden, call an unapproachable lion باسل, and call the ruqyah practitioner’s fee بسلته.
rows.anchor: والعرب تقول: أعط الراقي بسلته

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق وامرأته
rows.claim: Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq and his wife called their son ʿAbd al-Raḥmān to Islam, saying “Come to us, to the guidance,” that is, obey us.
rows.anchor: كان أبو بكر الصديق وامرأته يدعوان عبد الرحمن ابنهما إلى الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can also be read as إلى الهدى أن ائتنا; Arabic may include أن after أرسلنا or omit it.
rows.anchor: يجيء بأن، ويطرحها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وأن أقيموا الصلاة coordinates with the ل in وأمرنا لنسلم; أن is subjunctive as the second form of the command, like أمرتك لتذهب وأن تذهب.
rows.anchor: فأن في موضع نصب بالرد على الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation limits فيكون to the trumpet: God tells the trumpet to be on the day it is blown.
rows.anchor: يقال إن قوله: فيكون للصور خاصة، أي يوم يقول للصور: كن فيكون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another takes كن فيكون as a description of the true saying; that saying comes to pass on the day the trumpet is blown.
rows.anchor: كن فيكون لقوله هو الحق من نعت القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading makes كن فيكون apply to everything on that Day, treating the phrase as a complete clause, with القول بالحق raised and اليوم as its time expression.
rows.anchor: ويوم يقول كن فيكون لكل شيء فتكون كلمة مكتفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs say نفخ في الصور and نفخ; ʿAbd Allāh’s reading in the bird passage has فأنفخها فتكون طيرا بإذني. The cited rajaz line witnesses the phrase ينفخ الصور.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله: كهيئة الطير فأنفخها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say الصور is a horn; others take it as the plural of صورة, into which the dead are blown.
rows.anchor: ويقال: إن الصور قرن، ويقال: هو جمع للصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āzar is genitive but diptote as a foreign name; genealogists agree he was the son of Tāraḥ, so Āzar was likely a title.
rows.anchor: يقال: آزر في موضع خفض ولا يجرى لأنه أعجمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Āzar means crooked in their language, alluding to his deviation from the truth; another reading has the name in the nominative as a vocative and is good Arabic.
rows.anchor: وقد بلغني أن معنى (آزر) في كلامهم معوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In أتتخذ أصناما آلهة, أصناما is the direct object of the verb, and آلهة is likewise accusative.
rows.anchor: نصبت الأصنام بإيقاع الفعل عليها، وكذلك الآلهة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative من is nominative when it is the subject of قام, but accusative when it is the object of ضربت.
rows.anchor: ما أدرى من قام، ترفع (من) بقام، وما أدري من ضربت، تنصبها بضربت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The outward sins are sexual immorality and adultery; inward sin is illicit intimacy, when a woman takes a lover or a man takes her as one.
rows.anchor: فأما ظاهره فالفجور والزنى، وأما باطنه فالمخالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eating what was not consecrated to God is fisq, meaning unbelief; the wording alludes to the eating, just as “it increased them in faith” alludes to people’s words increasing their faith.
rows.anchor: يقول: أكلكم ما لم يذكر اسم الله عليه فسق أي كفر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dead person brought to life was astray and then guided; the light by which he walks among people is his faith.
rows.anchor: أي كان ضالا فهديناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exegetes understand صغار عند الله as humiliation from God; Arabic عندك can similarly mean من عندك, though one cannot say جئت عند زيد intending من عند زيد.
rows.anchor: أي من عند الله، كذلك قال المفسرون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible sense is that the disbelievers chose unbelief out of pride and disdain for following Muḥammad, so God made that choice a humiliation before Him.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون قوله: صغار عند الله أنهم اختاروا الكفر تعززا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿUmar read حَرَجا, while the common reading is حَرِجا; Ibn ʿAbbās glosses it as dense woodland inaccessible to grazing animals, like a disbeliever’s chest inaccessible to wisdom.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس وعمر (حرجا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two vocalizations share a meaning, like the paired forms الوحد/الوحد, الفرد/الفرد, and الدنف/الدنف.
rows.anchor: وهو في كسره وفتحه بمنزلة الوحد والوحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صاعد in كأنما يصعد في السماء describes someone whose path has narrowed until ascending into the sky seems the only way out, though he cannot do it; the verb is also read يصاعد or lightened يصعد.
rows.anchor: يقول: ضاق عليه المذهب فلم يجد إلا أن يصعد في السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn have led many people astray, which is what قد استكثرتم means here.
rows.anchor: يقول: قد أضللتم كثيرا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans benefited from jinn by seeking a valley’s lord for protection when alone or fearful after hunting; jinn benefited from the reverence humans showed them and boasted that they ruled both jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: أن الرجل كان إذا فارق فاستوحش أو قتل صيدا من صيدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With genitive أمثالها, the phrase means ten good deeds equal to it; عشر مثلها, ten good deeds like it, is also correct. أمثال is an attribute of عشر, and مثل can be singular or plural, as in إنكم إذا مثلهم and ثم لا يكونوا أمثالكم.
rows.anchor: من خفض يريد: فله عشر حسنات أمثالها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good deed is لا إله إلا الله and the evil deed is shirk.
rows.anchor: من جاء بالحسنة: بلا إله إلا الله، والسيئة: الشرك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In دينا قيما, دينا is an accusative verbal noun; ملة إبراهيم is likewise accusative in apposition or as a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: منصوب على المصدر. وملة إبراهيم كذلك.

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Ḥudhayfa told his son, whom he saw bowing with his head lowered, to raise his head and pray دينا قيما.
rows.anchor: أبي حذيفة راكعا قد صوبت رأسي، قال ارفع رأسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made Muḥammad’s community successors to all earlier communities and raised some people above others in provision to test them through what He gave.
rows.anchor: جعلت أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم خلائف كل الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لأقعدن لهم صراطك means I will sit for them on or in their path; the preposition is omitted because the path functions adverbially, as in قعدت لك وجه الطريق and temporal expressions such as غدا.
rows.anchor: المعنى- والله أعلم-: لاقعدن لهم على طريقهم أو في طريقهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رياشا may be a plural of ريش or a verbal noun meaning ريش, like لبس and لباس; the cited poem uses اللبس in this sense.
rows.anchor: كما يقال لبس ولباس قال الشاعر : فلما كشفن اللبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers reading لباس in the accusative, coordinated with ريش; in his reading that خير is raised by ذلك, while Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh read ولباس التقوى خير.
rows.anchor: وهي في قراءة أبي وعبد الله جميعا: ولباس التقوى خير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Just as God began creation with people either wretched or blessed, they will return in corresponding states of wretchedness or blessedness.
rows.anchor: يقول: بدأكم في الخلق شقيا وسعيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فريقا can be accusative under تعودون; Ubayy reads تعودون فريقين, while nominative forms are also sound, as in the verses about the two armies and the people of Paradise and Hell.
rows.anchor: ونصب الفريق بتعودون، وهي في قراءة أبي: تعودون فريقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse makes the first فريقا the object of هدى and the second accusative through a verb applying to its referent, as in والظالمين أعد لهم عذابا أليما.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون الفريق منصوبا بوقوع «هدى» عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أقيموا وجوهكم عند كل مسجد means to pray at any mosque where prayer time catches one; outside prayer time, one may pray wherever one wishes.
rows.anchor: إذا أدركتك الصلاة وأنت عند مسجد فصل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The calf was a hollow body, and exegetes say it lowed once.
rows.anchor: كان جسدا مجوفا. وجاء في التفسير أنه خار مرة واحدة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سقط في أيديهم means they regretted their deed; أسقط is also a dialect, but سقط في أيديهم is more frequent and better.
rows.anchor: من الندامة. ويقال: أسقط لغة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the direct address لئن لم ترحمنا ربنا over passive لئن لم يرحمنا ربنا, since ʿAbd Allāh’s codex places ربنا before the plea as a vocative.
rows.anchor: لأنها في مصحف عبد الله (قالوا ربنا لئن لم ترحمنا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عجلت الشيء means to get ahead of something, whereas أعجلته means to urge or hurry it.
rows.anchor: عجلت الشيء: سبقته، وأعجلته استحثثته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Moses broke two tablets, Arabic can use the plural الألواح for two, as with إخوة for two brothers and قلوبكما for two hearts.
rows.anchor: وجاز أن يقال الألواح للاثنين كما قال فإن كان له إخوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The frequent vocative ابن أم drops the possessive yāʾ and behaves like an accusative vocative (as in يا حسرتا); this wording softens Aaron, who was Moses’ full brother.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال له (يا ابن أم) ليستعطفه عليه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid read فلا تشمت بي; al-Kisāʾī wonders whether the intended wording is فلا تشمت بي الأعداء, and says the form may be sound because similar vowel variants occur in Arabic.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد أنه قرأ (فلا تشمت بي)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In either تشمت or تشمت, الأعداء is nominative because the enemies perform the verb.
rows.anchor: و (الأعداء) رفع لأن الفعل لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اختار موسى قومه سبعين means he chose seventy men from among his people: omitting من is allowed because the genitive construction خير القوم conveys the same meaning as خير من القوم. Two cited poems attest choosing a man as direct object.
rows.anchor: وجاء التفسير: اختار منهم سبعين رجلا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses thought the seventy had been destroyed for their companions’ calf worship, but they were struck by the quake because they asked him to show them God openly.
rows.anchor: فظن موسى أنهم أهلكوا باتخاذ أصحابهم العجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people in this passage disbelieved as Pharaoh’s people had disbelieved, and the same kind of punishment came upon them.
rows.anchor: يريد: كذب هؤلاء كما كذب آل فرعون، فنزل بهم كما نزل بآل فرعون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If captured, the enemy should be made an example for those behind them who may break their covenant, so that the latter remember and refrain; the kasra reading of من خلفهم has no interpretation he prefers.
rows.anchor: يريد: إن أسرتهم يا محمد فنكل بهم من خلفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means the enemy should be made to remember and not break the covenant; the kasra reading of من خلفهم has no interpretation he prefers.
rows.anchor: لعلهم يذكرون فلا ينقضون العهد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خيانة means breach of covenant; فانبذ إليهم بالنقض على سواء means respond openly as they did, or act publicly rather than secretly.
rows.anchor: يقول: نقض عهد فانبذ إليهم بالنقض على سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تخافن is jussive. Arabic rarely attaches emphatic nūn to a conditional unless it is joined with ما; إما was given nūn to distinguish the conditional from the choice form, and responses usually take فـ because إما is placed at the start, as in أما أخوك فقاعد.
rows.anchor: ولا تكاد العرب تدخل النون الشديدة ولا الخفيفة في الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard reading has the second-person verb; Ḥamza reads the third person, apparently following ʿAbd Allāh’s codex, which includes أنهم after يحسبن.
rows.anchor: بالتاء لا اختلاف فيها. وقد قرأها حمزة بالياء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without أنهم, the verb of supposing has no object; the alternative sense “do not suppose they cannot escape” works if لا is extra, as in the verse saying a destroyed town will not return (meaning it will return). With أن, one could say ولا يحسب الذين كفروا أن سبقوا.
rows.anchor: فإذا لم تكن فيها (أنهم) لم يستقم للظن ألا يقع على شيء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: موطئا means ground trodden; every valley crossed while going or returning is recorded for the believers.
rows.anchor: يريد بالموطئ الأرض ولا يقطعون واديا في ذهابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Muslims were blamed for staying behind from Tabūk, the Prophet’s expeditions left him alone; the verse says they should not all depart, but leave a group to learn revelation and teach it to those who stayed.
rows.anchor: لما عير المسلمون بتخلفهم عن غزوة تبوك جعل النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولينذروا means that the learned group should instruct their people in religion.
rows.anchor: ولينذروا قومهم يقول: ليفقهوهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says Bedouins of Asad came to Medina, raising prices and filling roads with filth; the verse then urged a group to learn and return to inform their people.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل فيها: إن أعراب أسد قدموا على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يلونكم من الكفار means the nearest enemies first, then those next nearest.
rows.anchor: يريد: الاقرب فالاقرب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites ask one another whether a new sūra increased their faith; the following contrast says it increases believers’ faith but adds defilement to those whose مرض means hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: يعني: المنافقين يقول بعضهم لبعض: هل زادتكم هذه إيمانا؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is read أولا يرون and also with second-person تاء; ʿAbd Allāh reads أو لا ترى أنهم. ألا ترى can address one or a group as an exclamation, like ذلك/ذلكم.
rows.anchor: أولا يرون (126) (وترون) بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a sūra exposing them is revealed, hypocrites ask whether anyone sees them if they leave; if they can slip away unseen, they do. ثم انصرفوا صرف الله قلوبهم is a curse against them.
rows.anchor: فيها ذكرهم وعيبهم قال بعضهم لبعض هل يراكم من أحد إن قمتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رسول من أنفسكم means no Arab clan was left without having given birth to him, so the messenger belongs to them.
rows.anchor: يقول: لم يبق بطن من العرب إلا وقد ولدوه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both occurrences of من are nominative because سواء governs them: whoever speaks secretly or openly, God knows him; it also means the visible and hidden are equal to Him.
rows.anchor: الذي رفعهما جميعا سواء، ومعناهما: أن من أسر القول أو جهر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The معقبات are angels: night angels follow day angels to guard the person. The word is grammatically masculine though it is a plural of the collective ملائكة معقبة, itself pluralized, like أبناوات سعد and رجالات.
rows.anchor: المعقبات: الملائكة، ملائكة الليل تعقب ملائكة النهار يحفظونه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine يحفظونه resumes the semantic meaning of معقبات; من أمر الله is fronted, or means their protection is by God’s command and permission, like acting because someone called.
rows.anchor: فرجع إلى التذكير الذي أخبرتك وهو المعنى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lightning inspires fear in the traveler and hope in the person staying at home.
rows.anchor: خوفا على المسافر وطمعا للحاضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about cattle has خلقها, while الخيل والبغال are nominative.
rows.anchor: والأنعام خلقها، والخيل والبغال على الرفع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads زينة as an accusative with an omitted verb meaning “make them an adornment,” as with حفظا; without واو before the purpose phrase, it could be governed by the preceding verb. Similarly, أعطيتك درهما ورغبة means I gave it to you wanting reward.
rows.anchor: ننصبها: ونجعلها زينة على فعل مضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قصد السبيل is explained as guidance of roads, and السبيل as Islam; ومنها جائر refers to Judaism and Christianity, supported by the following statement that God could guide everyone.
rows.anchor: يقال: هداية الطرق. ويقال السبيل، الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تسيمون means that you pasture your camels.
rows.anchor: تسيمون [10] ترعون إبلكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مواخر is the plural of ماخرة, the sound of ships moving through wind; the verb has the forms مخرت تمخر and تمخر.
rows.anchor: واحدها ماخرة وهو صوت جري الفلك بالرياح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stars used for navigation are identified as al-Jady and al-Farqadān.
rows.anchor: يقال: الجدي والفرقدان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من may refer to a nonhuman in أفمن يخلق because the created entity is paired with the Creator; the phrase about animals also uses من, and Arabic uses it for a rider and his mount when treated together.
rows.anchor: جعل (من) لغير الناس لما ميزه فجعله مع الخالق وصلح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أموات غير أحياء can be nominative as an independent clause or as the predicate of الذين; idols are literally lifeless. It may also be accusative as a result of the verb, meaning they make dead, lifeless things.
rows.anchor: رفعته بالاستئناف. وإن شئت رددته إلى أنه خبر للذين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the verse says they forgot their fish, only one forgot it, as the later statement to Moses says “I forgot the fish”; likewise, pearls and coral are said to emerge from two seas though they come only from the salt sea.
rows.anchor: وإنما نسيه واحد ألا ترى أنه قال لموسى (فإني نسيت الحوت)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أعطى كل شيء خلقه may mean that God gave every creature its mate or kind: a human male a woman, a sheep a sheep, and a bull a cow.
rows.anchor: يقال: أعطى الذكر من الناس امرأة مثله من صنفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثم هدى means that He inspired the male toward the female to be approached.
rows.anchor: وقوله: (ثم هدى) ألهم الذكر المأتى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لا يضل ربي means that God does not forget; ربي is nominative, with an omitted pronoun as the object of يضله in the coordinated لا ينسى.
rows.anchor: أي لا ينساه و (ربي) في موضع رفع تضمر الهاء في يضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أضللت describes something that escaped and became lost, like an animal; ضللته has two dialectal forms for misplacing a fixed object such as a house, and is not said with أضللت.
rows.anchor: وتقول: أضللت الشيء إذا ضاع مثل الناقة والفرس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أزواجا من نبات شتى describes plants differing in color and taste.
rows.anchor: أزواجا من نبات شتى [53] مختلف الألوان الطعوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs for people of understanding lie in the plants’ differing colors and tastes; ذو نهية means a person of intellect.
rows.anchor: يقول: في اختلاف ألوانه وطعمه آيات لذوي العقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تارة أخرى refers back to منها خلقناكم, not نعيدكم, since أخرى refers to a like kind; the parallel phrases are منها أخرجناكم and نخرجكم بعد الموت مرة أخرى.
rows.anchor: مردودة على قوله (منها خلقناكم) لا مردودة على (نعيدكم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فاجعل بيننا وبينك موعدا means set a time or deadline, which he then set.
rows.anchor: يقول: اضرب بيننا أجلا فضرب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مكانا سوى and سوى are Arabic; the most common form is سواء with fatḥ and a long vowel when it means middle or equal, as in the verse كلمة سواء. Kasra and ḍamma forms are also Arabic but shortened, and are read as such.
rows.anchor: إذا كان في معنى نصف وعدل فتحوه ومدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes say يوم الزينة was the people’s holiday; another view is that it was a market day when they adorned themselves.
rows.anchor: ذكر أنه جعل موعدهم يوم عيد، ويقال: يوم سوق كانت تكون لهم
